metadata.title: 게임수학 Part 2 · 다각형 ① 목적에 맞는 중심과 경계
metadata.description:
게임에서 가운데 점은 무엇을 위해 고를까요? 좌표를 평균한 무게중심, 변까지 같은 거리에 있는 내심, 꼭짓점까지 같은 거리에 있는 외심을 같은 작은 삼각형으로 비교합니다. 이후 타일 배치, 건축, 화면의 대상 표시, 동굴 통로를 통해 한 점과 전체 경계가 다른 정보임을 확인합니다. 순서 있는 경계와 볼록·오목을 검사하고, 삼각형 분할은 다음 편으로 이어갑니다. 기존 설명과 계산을 보존하고 게임 사이의 비교를 추가한 다각형 강의 첫 번째 편입니다.

https://www.yamyamcoding.com/1ea0b1ff-a61e-803f-bd54-cac4f028f6b3

englishMetadata.title: Game Math Part 2 · Polygons1: Centers and Boundaries
englishMetadata.description:
What should a center point represent in a game? Using the same small triangle, compare the coordinate-average centroid, the incenter at equal distances from sides, and the circumcenter at equal distances from vertices. Tile placement, building edits, screen target markers and cave passages then show why one reference point differs from a complete boundary. Validate boundary order and distinguish convexity from concavity; the following episode continues with triangle partitioning. This first polygon lecture preserves the original explanations and calculations while adding comparisons across games.

Game Math PART2 course materials
https://www.yamyamcoding.com/1ea0b1ff-a61e-803f-bd54-cac4f028f6b3

YamYamCoding website
https://www.yamyamcoding.com/

YamYamWiki course notes
https://www.yamyamcoding.com/0d2adf45-5d1a-43be-a37c-61c94b1ae2c8

40% actual gameplay and60% explanation, narrated without background music.

Chapters
00:00 Choose centers for a purpose and retain the boundary
00:13 Overview of centers and polygon partitioning
00:39 The scope of these two episodes
00:49 Observe tile placement and a reference point
01:37 Equal weights give the coordinate average
01:52 Three centers answer three different questions
02:29 What does a centroid average?
03:12 A placement reference differs from the full outline
03:40 Observe a target and its visible outline
04:31 Why angle bisectors give equal distances to sides
04:53 Compute the same incenter and radius
05:35 Why perpendicular bisectors start at side midpoints
05:50 Circumcenter and outside-center cases
06:37 A doorway retains empty space
06:58 Observe terrain and open passages
07:55 Join points to define the land to retain
08:08 Validate the boundary before partitioning
08:49 Convexity and concavity
09:28 Separate height changes from a planar notch
09:55 Tile boundaries, holes and convexity
10:48 Compare reference points and outlines across games
11:16 Test terrain boundaries in other cave intervals
11:44 A turn test and its conditions
12:00 Convexity tests and angle-sum limits
12:47 A valid boundary motivates triangle partitioning
13:02 Membership thanks and programming coaching
